images.title: One centimetre cut into ten parts
images.purpose: Show that 1 cm is cut into 10 equal parts of 1 mm with 9 small marks, as seen through a lens on a ruler.
images.composition: A strip of a ruler at the top with a circle on one centimetre, and the magnified centimetre below it with its ten parts.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. RULER STRIP: one yellow rectangle 600 px wide and 80 px high (x 128 to 728, y 120 to 200) with exactly 4 tall tick marks at x 128, 248, 368 and 488 (long, 40 px) labelled 1, 2, 3 and 4 below the ticks in 36 px, and short ticks between them. LENS: one circle 120 px across with a thick reddish purple #CC79A7 outline around the part from the 1 mark to the 2 mark (centre x 188, y 160), joined by two thin grey #6B7280 lines to the ends of the magnified bar below. MAGNIFIED BAR: one yellow rectangle 1000 px wide and 120 px high (x 228 to 1228, y 330 to 450) with exactly 11 tick marks, one every 100 px from x 228 to x 1228, the first and the last tall (70 px) and the other 9 short (40 px), so 10 equal parts. Above the bar a teal #0072B2 bracket from x 228 to x 328 at y 300 with the label 1 mm in 40 px at x 278, y 260. Under the bar a green #009E73 bracket from x 228 to x 1228 at y 500 with the label 1 cm = 10 mm in 56 px bold at x 728, y 560. At the right, in 40 px, 9 small marks at x 1290, y 390. In all: 1 ruler strip, 1 lens, 1 magnified bar, 11 ticks, 2 brackets. All shapes are flat fills with thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (3 px), no shadows and no gradients; all text is dark #1F2937 sans-serif. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 11 ticks on the magnified bar
images.takeaway: 1 cm is cut into 10 equal parts of 1 mm, and there are 9 small marks between two cm marks.
images.description: A lens on 1 cm of a ruler and the magnified centimetre with its ten equal parts of 1 mm, written 1 cm = 10 mm.
images.context: Concept image for The Millimetre. It follows the idea of the ruler picture in your maths book (one centimetre divided into ten equal parts, each 1 mm) and shows the ruler's own marks.
images.teaching_notes: Count the 9 small marks with the child. The slip to watch: counting 10 marks, the two ends included.

image_decisions.why: Show that 1 cm is cut into 10 equal parts of 1 mm with 9 small marks, as seen through a lens on a ruler.
